note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Acute diarrheal illness with fever and vomiting for 3 days.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptoms began 3 days ago; currently ongoing.
- Symptoms details:
  - Diarrhea: very loose stools; started watery, now very loose; today at least four bowel movements.
  - Fever: patient reports feeling feverish, “boiling” to touch; no thermometer available.
  - Nausea/vomiting: recurrent vomiting, cannot keep fluids or solids down; last episode approximately 2 hours ago after breakfast.
  - Abdominal pain: central periumbilical area; tender to touch; pain comes and goes with urge to stool.
  - Urine: urinating; last void about 1 hour ago; color not documented; no blood in urine.
  - Stool blood: none reported.
- Past medical history: Normally healthy; no prior abdominal problems; regular menstrual cramps.
- Medications: Vitamin D daily; intermittent ibuprofen for cramps (dose/route/frequency not documented); ORS (oral rehydration salts) used ~3 times daily for past 2 days.
- Allergies: Not stated.
- Social history: Graphics designer; lives with mother and brother; non-smoker; occasional alcohol; missed work (working from home); not using contraception; regular sexual activity not applicable.
- Exposures: Brother with similar symptoms; possible infectious gastroenteritis; not abroad.

Objective:
- Vital signs: Not documented.
- Physical examination: Not documented.
- Hydration/urine: Urinated last ~1 hour ago; color not documented; no blood in urine.
- Stool/urinalysis: Not performed; stool testing discussed/planned.
- Additional: No documented fever measurement; patient reports fever by sensation.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Infectious gastroenteritis with dehydration risk (probable viral etiology; bacterial infection not ruled out)
   - Assessment: Suspected infectious gastroenteritis; dehydration risk due to vomiting and inability to keep fluids down.
   - Differential diagnoses: Viral gastroenteritis; bacterial gastroenteritis; other causes of acute diarrhea less likely given history.
   - Investigations planned: Stool sample to screen for bacterial infection; ongoing assessment of hydration.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Continue oral rehydration salts with small, frequent sips (to minimize vomiting).
     - Light, easily digestible foods (toast or biscuits) when able; avoid fruit, vegetables, milk initially.
     - Monitor hydration status; if symptoms worsen or fail to improve, pursue urgent evaluation in A&E.
     - Clinic visit arranged as an urgent appointment to obtain stool sample and assess hydration.
   - Referrals: Urgent clinic appointment for testing and hydration assessment; A&E referral if condition worsens.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies not documented.
  - Medication reconciliation incomplete (ibuprofen dose/route/frequency not documented; ORS dosing not specified).
  - Vitals and detailed physical examination not documented.
  - Specific stool test results not available (planned rather than completed).
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Moderately clear; some repetition and interruptions, but key clinical information is present.
